title: Signal Blocks Screenshots to Keep Gemini and Siri Out of Your Chats
dek: Signal calls OS-level AI agents an "existential threat" to app privacy.

facts.label: No block yet, manual workaround needed

caption:
Your phone's AI assistant might be reading your private messages. Signal just drew a line. 🔒

On November 20, 2026, Signal started blocking screenshots inside its app so built-in AI agents like Google Gemini Intelligence on Android and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI on Apple devices can't read your chats. iOS 27 gets the block by default, and Android turns on Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen. Mac users still need to add Signal to Siri's Excluded Apps list manually.

Why it matters: encryption only protects messages in transit. Once a message is on your screen, an OS agent can capture it and send it elsewhere. Signal president Meredith Whittaker is now asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for a real, documented way for apps to opt out of AI data access.

We're following this privacy fight closely at AI Parabellum. Would you turn screenshots back on, knowing it affects your contacts too?

post_caption:
Encryption means little if the operating system can read your screen. That's Signal's argument as it blocks screenshots to stop Gemini and Siri AI agents from scanning private chats.

The fix is partial, with gaps on Mac and some Android phones, but the bigger ask is clear: Apple, Google and Microsoft need to let apps opt out of AI data access. 📱
